title: Losing weight after 50: what changes and what still works
intro: After 50, many people feel weight is harder to lose. That is normal, not your fault. The body does change. But the good news is, simple and consistent habits still work. You don't need a strict diet or to train like an athlete. You can keep eating rice and your favourite dishes, just rearrange things little by little.

sections.p: Muscle decreases if we move less. With less muscle, the body uses slightly less energy every day. Sleep may also be disturbed. Some medicines can also affect appetite or body weight. So if you eat as much as you did at 30, your weight can easily creep up.

Portion size still matters most. Reduce your rice a little, add vegetables, and make sure there is a protein dish. Cut down on sweet drinks, because they easily add energy without making you feel full. Small changes made every day work better than big changes that only last a week.

Protein helps protect muscle and keeps you full longer. Examples are fish, eggs, skinless chicken, tofu, tempeh, dhal and low-fat milk. Try to have a palm-sized portion of protein at every main meal. This is a simple estimate, no need to weigh.

Walking is the best exercise for many people. Start with 10 minutes, then add slowly. To strengthen your muscles, try sit-to-stand from a chair and wall push-ups. No need to jump or run. If your knees hurt, go slower and use a smaller range of movement.

At this age, weight usually comes down more slowly. That does not mean you have failed. Look at other signs too, like looser clothes, climbing stairs more easily or having more energy. Try to sleep at the same time every night, because lack of sleep can make us hungrier the next day.

action: Reduce your rice to about one scoop, and add one type of vegetable to your plate.
Make sure there is a protein dish like fish, egg or tofu at every lunch and dinner.
Swap one sweet drink a day for kosong (no sugar) or kurang manis (less sweet).
Walk for 10 minutes after eating, for example around the park or inside the house.
Do 5 to 10 sit-to-stands from a chair, once a day.
doctor: See a doctor first before starting exercise or changing how you eat if you have chest pain, breathlessness or dizziness when moving, heart disease, high blood pressure or diabetes that is not yet controlled, swollen and hot knees, a recent fall, or are taking medicine for sugar, blood pressure or the heart. Do not change or stop your medicine on your own. Discuss with your doctor.

faq.q: Is it true my metabolism is broken after 50?
faq.a: It's not broken. It just changes a little, mainly because muscle decreases. By eating enough protein and moving every day, you can still help your body use energy well.

faq.q: Do I need to join a gym?
faq.a: No need. Walking, chair exercises and wall push-ups at home are enough to start. What matters is doing it often, not doing it hard.

faq.q: Can I skip dinner to lose weight faster?
faq.a: Not recommended, especially if you take medicine for blood sugar or blood pressure. It's better to have a light dinner with vegetables and protein, and reduce your rice a little.
